baseline.disclaimer: Any-photo baseline is not publication-ready coverage; 12 provisional pilot heroes remain unapproved. These B21 leads do not change counts.

policy: One image of exact physical object (or defined set) only; plain neutral background; correct historic Latin Catholic usage; verify image-level rights and full-size framing; no release without human QA.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Silver-gilt sunburst monstrance, attributed to Diego de Atienza, Lima, 1646–49; Mercedarian commission for a Spanish parish.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Expensive historic sunburst exemplar, not necessarily representative of a humble 1962 parish; original pixel check and curator acceptance required.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Spanish silver pyx, late 15th–early 16th c.; Met explicitly identifies reserved consecrated Host use.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Historic larger pyx, do not use for SA11 home-Communion pyx-and-case unless matched case is actually photographed.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Spanish or Portuguese late-17th/early-18th-century ecclesiastical antependium in silk, metal and linen.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Do not adopt if original photograph crops portions of the complete textile. Met 462800 visually shows full object but British pre-Reformation provenance needs separate historical QA.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Italian Tuscan sacristy cupboard, walnut, ca. 1490–1500.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Historic cupboard, grayscale reproduction; prefer a colour isolated complete press if found.
Historic single combined vessel; 201835 is museum-catalogued Chrismatory (?) only, so do not automatically prefer it due to the attribution question mark.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Italian Roman gilt bronze liturgical pax showing Risen Christ appearing to Apostles, probably Guglielmo della Porta, 1566–77.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Historically documented Roman-rite ceremonial object; differentiate from modern sign of peace and do not imply normally employed at every 1962 Mass.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Actual holy-oil ambry in Roman Catholic San Pancrazio, Ancignano, Veneto, photographed 2025.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Architecture is part of in-situ wall-mounted ambry; crop cannot imply free-standing object. Attribution and share-alike required.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Montreal holy-water aspersorium, silver, 1811, attributed to silversmith Pierre Huguet dit Latour.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: Source specifically aspersorium, not generic incense bucket; museum web image visibly exists but complete isolation/full-resolution still to inspect.

new_gap_subject_leads.identity: Quebec religious aspergillum, 1811, approximately 25cm, separate companion artifact to M10979.1.
new_gap_subject_leads.caveat: The two companion artifacts MUST NOT be combined in one hero photograph; each has its own museum page with its own image.

other_verified_research.reason: Object museum-classified lectern, not a confirmed Roman Catholic altar Missal stand. Do not supersede LACMA BK02 hold merely on resemblance.

other_verified_research.identity: Catholic holy-water bucket with aspergillum shown together.
other_verified_research.reason: Two separately catalogued objects in one photograph violate single-object hero rule, even with image rights recorded.

other_verified_research.identity: A.W.N. Pugin / J. Hardman hanging sanctuary lamp, photographed by Daderot at the Huntington.
other_verified_research.reason: Museum environment and no familiar red glass; not a satisfactory SN05 primary.

other_verified_research.identity: Andalusian Catholic baptismal shell, IAPH photograph 2022
other_verified_research.reason: Object type and professional photograph identified, but noncommercial clause prevents free commercial reuse; maintain rights hold.

other_verified_research.identity: 18th-century New Spanish silver baptismal shell, Museum Amparo collection
other_verified_research.reason: Excellent correct isolated object lead with photography rights not yet confirmed; no asset import.
